newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Syria must decide if it wants peace - Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Syria must decide if it wants peace - Netanyahu.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday Syria had to decide itself if it wanted to resume peace talks with the Jewish state.

"I don't expect Washington to bring Syria to the negotiating table. That's a Syrian decision," Netanyahu said during a stopover en route to the United States for talks with U.S. President Bill Clinton and members of his administration.
Stalled peace talks with Syria are expected to feature prominently during his talks at the White House on Thursday.

"Syria has to make a decision. Does it want peace. If it wants peace it can come to the peace table very quickly. If it doesn't want peace it will find ways to obstruct the resumption of the talks," he told reporters at Amsterdam airport.
The U.S. is expected to try to get Israel and Syria to revive peace talks which Israel broke off after a series of Islamist suicide bombings in Israel a year ago.
But the two countries remain at loggerheads over the Golan Heights captured by Israel from Syria in 1967.
Syria demands the return of the strategic plateau but Netanyahu opposes a "land for peace" deal.
Clinton and Netanyahu last met in October 1996, in talks which also involved Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
Netanyahu held brief talks in Amsterdam with Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and said he would return to the Netherlands on April 10 for fuller talks with Kok.
The Netherlands holds the presidency of the European Union during the first half of this year.
